3. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
4. use crate::mm::phys::FrameAllocView;
5. 
6. // `Result::and_then`: on `Ok`, the closure is applied to the payload (its precondition must hold);
7. // on `Err`, the error is forwarded unchanged. Mirrors `core`'s implementation. vstd ships no
8. // specification for it.
9. pub assume_specification<T, E, U, F: FnOnce(T) -> Result<U, E>>[ Result::<T, E>::and_then ](
10.     result: Result<T, E>,
11.     op: F,
12. ) -> (res: Result<U, E>)
13.     requires
14.         result is Ok ==> op.requires((result->Ok_0,)),
15.     ensures
16.         result is Err ==> res == Err::<U, E>(result->Err_0),
17.         result is Ok ==> op.ensures((result->Ok_0,), res),
18. ;
19. 
20. // `Result::inspect_err`: runs a side-effecting closure on the error (if any) and returns the
21. // receiver unchanged. The closure is used purely for its effects, so no abstract obligation is
22. // threaded. vstd ships no specification for it.
23. pub assume_specification<T, E, F: FnOnce(&E)>[ Result::<T, E>::inspect_err ](
24.     result: Result<T, E>,
25.     f: F,
26. ) -> (res: Result<T, E>)
27.     ensures
28.         res == result,
29. ;
30. 
31. // `Vec::capacity`: reports spare storage; opaque with respect to the abstract sequence. vstd
32. // ships no specification for it.
33. pub assume_specification<T, A: ::core::alloc::Allocator>[ Vec::<T, A>::capacity ](
34.     vec: &Vec<T, A>,
35. ) -> (c: usize)
36. ;
37. 
38. //==================================================================================================
39. // Build-time kernel watermark
40. //==================================================================================================
41. 
42. /// The kernel watermark: the number of physical frames the kernel always keeps free for itself.
43. ///
44. /// User allocations are gated by this threshold; kernel allocations bypass it. Mirrors the
45. /// build-time constant `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`, which is generated by the `config`
46. /// crate's `build.rs` (from `kernel_config.toml`) and therefore lives outside Verus's view.
47. /// The abstract value is fixed by the `external_body` accessor `kernel_watermark()`; this is an
48. /// external-bottom trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). Callers do not depend on
49. /// the concrete threshold — only on the fact that user allocations are gated by it.
50. pub uninterp spec fn spec_kernel_watermark() -> nat;
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // Allocation / watermark vocabulary (on the existing FrameAllocView)
54. //==================================================================================================
55. 
56. impl FrameAllocView {
57.     /// Number of frames currently free, i.e. available to hand out. This is the single quantity
58.     /// the kernel watermark reads. Models `frame::free_count()`.
59.     pub open spec fn free_count(self) -> nat {
60.         self.free_frames.len()
61.     }
62. 
63.     /// A user allocation of `count` frames is admissible: fulfilling it would still leave at
64.     /// least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames free for the kernel. This is the predicate behind the
65.     /// user-vs-kernel asymmetry that `check_user_watermark` enforces.
66.     pub open spec fn user_alloc_ok(self, count: nat) -> bool {
67.         self.free_count() >= count + spec_kernel_watermark()
68.     }
69.

71.     /// `allocated_frames` with refcount 1. (Equivalent to `book_all(set![addr])`.)
72.     pub open spec fn alloc_one(self, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
73.         FrameAllocView {
74.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
75.             free_frames: self.free_frames.remove(addr),
76.             refcounts: self.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
77.         }
78.     }
79. }

83. //==================================================================================================

86.     type V = FrameAllocView;
87. 
88.     /// The manager brokers the global physical-frame partition. Its abstract state is exactly
89.     /// that partition, realized here through the user page pool it owns; the attachment to the
90.     /// global frame allocator (`self@ == phys_view().frames`) is pinned in the proving phase.
91.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView {
92.         self.upool@
93.     }
94. }
95. 
96. impl PhysMemoryManager {
97.     /// Well-formedness invariant: the brokered frame partition is well formed (free/allocated
98.     /// disjoint, page-aligned, refcount <-> allocated consistent, refcounts in 1..=255).
99.     ///
100.     /// Liveness is structural (a `&mut self` is only obtainable after `init` succeeded) and the
101.     /// watermark is a per-user-allocation gate, not an invariant — kernel allocations are
102.     /// designed to dip below it — so neither appears here.
103.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
104.         self@.wf()
105.     }
106. }
107. 
108. //==================================================================================================
109. // Handle-set helpers
110. //==================================================================================================
111. 
112. /// The set of physical frame addresses owned by a sequence of user-frame handles.
113. pub open spec fn user_addr_set(frames: Seq<UserFrame>) -> Set<int> {
114.     Set::new(|a: int| exists|i: int| 0 <= i < frames.len() && #[trigger] frames[i]@ == a)
115. }
116.

118. pub open spec fn kernel_addr_set(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>) -> Set<int> {
119.     Set::new(|a: int| exists|i: int| 0 <= i < frames.len() && #[trigger] frames[i]@ == a)

123. /// run: there is a page-aligned `base` such that handle `i` owns `base + i * page_size`. This is the
124. /// identity-map contiguity guarantee that kernel-stack callers (`alloc_kpages`) depend on.

127.         #![trigger crate::mm::phys::region_frame_addrs(base, (count * spec_page_size()) as int)]

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the
  module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
  Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
  `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
  state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
  the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
  Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
  volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
  `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
  carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
  PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
  `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
  change).
- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
  Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
  `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
  `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
  index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
  contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
  `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
  `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
  slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
  **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
  `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
  `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
  entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
  verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
  page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
  `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
  state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
  so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
  `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
  This matches the inherited upstream
  `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
  `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
  `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.

17. /// Captures which physical frames are currently allocated vs. free,
18. /// together with a per-frame reference count that models shared

21. {
22.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,
23.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,
24.     /// Maps each allocated frame address to its reference count.
25.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated.
26.     pub refcounts: Map<int, int>,
27. }

31.     pub open spec fn wf(&self) -> bool
32.     {
33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
35.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
36.         // Disjoint
37.         &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)

45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
